page: Amazon Web Services d3en.6xlarge is a storage-optimized instance engineered for capacity-dense, high-throughput storage workloads. Operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Compute allocation includes 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, supported by 35 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory comprises 96 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, yielding an allocation of 4 GB per virtual core.

The primary defining characteristic of the d3en.6xlarge is its massive bundled local storage array, providing 167,760 GB of capacity across local HDDs. To sustain data movement into and out of this storage volume, the instance includes a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Accelerator hardware is absent, with zero GPUs allocated. The hardware profile is tuned specifically for high-capacity sequential data retention and distributed file system nodes rather than low-latency random access flash operations.

Benchmark evaluations indicate an average tier of multi-threaded execution, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,267 and PassMark CPU score of 20,039.62. Conversely, single-core execution ranks in the lower quartile, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,056 and lower single-threaded compression speeds. Memory bandwidth remains in average ranges, achieving 108.25 GB/sec on large uncached block reads and 47.85 GB/sec on block writes. Redis SET operations reached 20.06 million operations per second, with database operation benchmarks scoring within median bounds.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the d3en.6xlarge provides a vast storage volume per virtual core. Because the massive storage footprint is bundled on mechanical drives rather than solid-state media, it represents a cost-efficient deployment for storage-heavy architectures where capacity outweighs sub-millisecond IOPS requirements. Workload fit includes Hadoop and MapReduce distributed clusters, large-scale data lakes, sequential log processing, backup repositories, and high-volume archival file serving.
description: Amazon Web Services d3en.6xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor, the system provides 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores, 96 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, and an expansive 167,760 GB of local HDD storage. Network throughput is provisioned with a 40 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations place multi-core CPU capacity, memory throughput, and database operations in average percentiles, while single-core processing metrics, such as compression and text parsing, reside in lower tiers. The architecture exhibits a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, balancing processing capacity against extensive capacity-optimized local spindle storage. By prioritizing sheer storage density and sustained network throughput over top-tier single-thread performance, this instance delivers strong cost efficiency for distributed storage clusters, massive sequential log archives, data lakes, and high-capacity analytical processing pipelines.
